translationRepairs.reason: Packet s0090 reads 廆懼，首服, but CText Jinshu 載記第八 has 燾懼，首服 after Hui threatens nephew 燾; parallel editions likewise make Tao submit. Idiomatic "Bi" invents Cui Bi, and "Tao groveled in terror" restores the correct subject.
Same corrupt packet 廆懼; CText and parallel witnesses read 燾懼，首服, so the literal must name Tao, not Bi, as the one who submitted under threat.

translationRepairs.before: Hui's reign disasters enabled Shi Le.
translationRepairs.after: Late Emperor Hui's disasters enabled Shi Le.
translationRepairs.reason: 惠皇之末 names Western Jin Emperor Hui (惠皇), not Murong Hui; bare "Hui's reign" in this Murong chapter misidentifies the referent, and "Late Emperor Hui" matches 惠皇之末.

translationRepairs.before: Thereupon he composed the \Household Instructions\" in several thousand words to spell out these aims."
translationRepairs.after: Thereupon he composed the "Household Instructions" in several thousand words to spell out these aims.
translationRepairs.reason: Literal corrupts the title 《家令》 with broken backslash-escaped quotes and a stray trailing quote; restoring ordinary "Household Instructions" quotes fixes the field without changing sense.

translationRepairs.before: He promoted worthies to routine administration: Hedong Pei Yi, Dai commandery Lu Chang, Beiping Yang Dan as strategists; Beihai Feng Xian, Guangping You Sui, Beiping Fang Qian, Bohai Feng Chou, Xihe Song Shi, Hedong Pei Kai as arms and legs; Bohai Feng Yi, Pingyuan Song Gai, Anding Huangfu Qi, Lanling Miao Kai held literary portfolios; Kuaiji Zhu Zuoche, Taishan Humu Yi, Lu state Kong Zuan served as honored guests; Pingyuan Liu Zan's erudition made him Libationer of the eastern school where heir Huang studied.
translationRepairs.after: He promoted worthies to routine administration: Hedong Pei Yi, Dai commandery Lu Chang, Beiping Yang Dan as strategists; Beihai Feng Xian, Guangping You Sui, Beiping Xifang Qian, Bohai Feng Chou, Xihe Song Shi, Hedong Pei Kai as arms and legs; Bohai Feng Yi, Pingyuan Song Gai, Anding Huangfu Ji, Lanling Miao Kai held literary portfolios; Kuaiji Zhu Zuoche, Taishan Humu Yi, Lu state Kong Zuan served as honored guests; Pingyuan Liu Zan's erudition made him Libationer of the eastern school where heir Huang studied.
translationRepairs.reason: 北平西方虔 is the compound surname Xifang, so "Fang Qian" is wrong and the proposal's "Xifang Qian" is right; the same literal still misreads 皇甫岌 as "Huangfu Qi," which must be "Huangfu Ji" as in the idiomatic and name claims.

translationRepairs.before: Kan replied to Feng Chou's letter in gist: \General of Chariots and Cavalry forgets self for the state—tribute baskets crowd the road; Jie bandits sued peace yet he handed envoys to court; he struck west at Duan lands, campaigned north beyond the passes, soothed Suotou tribes—distant desert peoples submitted tribute.\
translationRepairs.after: Kan replied to Feng Chou's letter in gist: "General of Chariots and Cavalry forgets self for the state—tribute baskets crowd the road; Jie bandits sued peace yet he handed envoys to court; he struck west at Duan lands, campaigned north beyond the passes, soothed Suotou tribes—distant desert peoples submitted tribute."
translationRepairs.reason: Literal wraps Tao Kan's quoted gist in broken backslash escapes; restoring ordinary quotation marks around the 其略曰 speech fixes the corruption without altering content.

translationRepairs.before: Murong coordinated a joint petition southward.
translationRepairs.after: Later Hui rewrote his earlier letter and also sent with it a memorial from his Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, acting Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, and others, more than thirty men in all, addressed to Tao Kan’s headquarters, which said:
translationRepairs.reason: In 並齎…等三十餘人疏, 齎 means Hui also sent along the memorial (疏) of Feng Chou, Han Jiao and the others. 等三十餘人 is the total of signers, more than thirty including the named men, not thirty more besides them. The memorial belongs to those officers, not to Hui jointly, and nothing says they travelled. The proposal made Hui co-author and added 'more than thirty others'.

translationRepairs.before: Later Hui rewrote the earlier letter and together with Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, acting Liaodong minister Han Jiao, and thirty others memorialized Tao Kan's headquarters:
translationRepairs.after: Later Hui rewrote the earlier letter, and also sent the memorial of his Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, acting Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, and others, more than thirty men, submitted to Tao Kan's headquarters, saying:
translationRepairs.reason: Same parse as part-3-repair-0. 並齎 means 'also sent along'. The 疏 belongs to Feng Chou, Han Jiao and the others, with 等三十餘人 as the total ('more than thirty', not 'thirty others'). Hui did not co-memorialize. 其 ('his') is restored, and 相 becomes chancellor to match 109:s0018.

candidateDispositions.note: Eastern Yi is an ethnographic collective in the comparison with western Qiang, not Pei Yi.
Truncated title-and-surname detector expression overlaps the fully linked Feng Chou mention; 封抽 remains linked to jinshu:108:p038.
Office jurisdiction in Han Jiao’s acting Liaodong chancellorship (行遼東相), not another individual.
